123: def create_conversation_token(widget_id: str, customer_id: Optional[str] = None, customer_email: Optional[str] = None, **extra_data) -> str:
124:     """
125:     Create a JWT token for widget conversations with revocation support via Redis
126:     
127:     Includes a JTI (JWT ID) claim for revocation. Token is stored in Redis with TTL.
128:     Optionally stores customer email for session tracking and bulk revocation.
129:     
130:     Args:
131:         widget_id: The widget ID
132:         customer_id: Optional customer ID
133:         customer_email: Optional customer email for session management
134:         **extra_data: Additional data to include in token
135:     """
136:     jti = str(uuid.uuid4())
137:     data = {
138:         "widget_id": widget_id,
139:         "type": "conversation",
140:         "jti": jti
141:     }
142: 
143:     # Only include `sub` when a customer_id is present. RFC 7519 (and python-jose)
144:     # require `sub` to be a string — encoding it as JSON null causes decode to fail
145:     # with JWTError("Subject must be a string") for anonymous widget visitors
146:     # (e.g. Explore flow), which silently drops all downstream claims (like `source`).
147:     if customer_id is not None:
148:         data["sub"] = customer_id
149: 
150:     # Add email to token if provided
151:     if customer_email:
152:         data["email"] = customer_email
153:     
154:     # Add any extra data to the token
155:     data.update(extra_data)
156:     
157:     # Set expiration to 30 days
158:     now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
159:     expire = now + timedelta(days=30)
160:     data.update({"exp": expire})
161: 
162:     token = jwt.encode(data, CONVERSATION_SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)

71: > **The `certbot` service must stay one-shot — never give it a long-running
72: > loop entrypoint.** It previously used
73: > `sh -c 'trap exit TERM; while :; do certbot renew; sleep 12h & wait ${!}; done;'`,
74: > which broke renewal in two non-obvious ways:
75: >
76: > 1. **`compose run` inherits the entrypoint.** The "one-off" cron run never
77: >    exited, so `--rm` never fired (a container leaked *every night*) and the
78: >    cron's chained `&& nginx -s reload` never ran at all.
79: > 2. **`sh -c '<script>' <args>` silently discards the args** (they land in
80: >    `$0`/`$1`…, which the script ignores). So it renewed *without* the
81: >    `--deploy-hook`, every 12h — beating the daily cron to the renewal. The
82: >    cron's own `renew` then found nothing due, so the hook never fired.
83: >
84: > Net effect: certs renewed on disk while **nginx kept serving the old ones**,
85: > masked only by deploys happening to restart nginx. Left alone that expires a
86: > live cert. The service is therefore declared with no `entrypoint:` (the
87: > image's default is `certbot`) and `profiles: ["tools"]`, so `compose up -d`
88: > never starts it while `compose run` still works (it auto-enables the profile).
